review_reference: Coordinator in chat, 2026-11-04, for the owner's launch ("full speed for launch"): "0120 first (prove it, then fix), then the two Outreach blockers"; first numbered 0120 by the coordinator, renumbered 0110 on 2026-11-11 because production ends at 0108, 0109 (#213, support Health ID matches) releases first and the release contract requires a contiguous list. SIGNED by the owner, D-Eminence, in chat on 2026-11-11 (~01:15 UTC): "sign outreach fix".
evidence: In plain words, applying 0110 to production does this. Today every registration of a person into an Outreach campaign is refused, and the field officer sees a server error: the database check that a registration into a campaign is made by a member of that campaign tried to lock the member's row, and production's database settings (the migration login does not bypass row-level security, and campaign memberships have no update rule) made that lock find nothing, so even a real member was refused. Registrations without a campaign were never affected. 0110 changes that one check so it locks the campaign only and reads the membership without locking it. Every rule stays: only a member of the campaign may register into it, only at the campaign's own facility, only while the campaign is active and offers registration, and a registration's campaign cannot be changed afterwards; the refusals keep their codes and messages. A campaign being closed still waits for a registration in progress (and the other way round). Nothing is granted to anyone; no table, row-level security policy, role or permission changes; the Outreach service still cannot change or lock a campaign membership. Shipped in the same backend release: outreach-api answers a refusal that still comes from this check as its own check does (403 OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN_ACCESS_DENIED, 409 OUTREACH_CAMPAIGN_NOT_ACCEPTING_REGISTRATIONS) instead of 500. Today's outreach-api image works on 0110 unchanged. No down migration; rolling the images back leaves 0110 in place and the earlier image works with it. Technical record: 0110_outreach_campaign_registration_lock.sql (first numbered 0120), written on f11c9ec9 (production 0102-0105) and merged onto staging (0106 OCR worker account, 0107 OCR page allowance, 0108 records processing cover lifetime), is backward compatible. It applies after 0109 (support Health ID matches, #213) and uses nothing 0106-0109 add: none of 0106-0109 changes an object 0110 reads, pins or replaces (0108 replaces only identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover; 0109 only creates identity.support_health_id_matches(text[])); runtime-grants.sql's 0110 block follows the earlier blocks. It replaces only the body of outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write() (0045; md5 afabd66c378c6e076062f35e80de9cb2 to 69469315f04554d2639dfa9f83591d4d): FOR SHARE OF campaign instead of FOR SHARE OF campaign, member; language plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, platform, auth, identity, outreach, owner, ACL (owner only) and the trigger outreach_registration_campaign_validate unchanged; a comment on the function. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0110 block (revoke from PUBLIC on that function, as 0045 did; no grant changes). Preconditions (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501 with nothing applied): 0001-0109 applied, 0109's identity.support_health_id_matches(text[]) with body md5 e4f1577e17334abde24784ff9c5c6c66 as the marker; not applied yet; the replaced body and platform.current_membership_id 641989704fea95f885fbc38c6feb5aa5, outreach.context_allows(uuid,text) 1e0e660ba5fd9288f1c1aeca5a7137ac, platform.reject_mutation 398738f39f6eebed2c54da5009495def; the function's attributes; both triggers; the eleven columns read; the read and update policies relied on and no UPDATE or ALL policy on outreach.campaign_members; row-level security enabled and forced on the three tables; the applier is the owner or inherits it with SET. Post-checks: the new md5, attributes, owner, ACL, the trigger, still no UPDATE policy. Locks: SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the function, catalog read locks and the session's own temporary objects; no application table. Proof: measured 2026-11-11 on throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 clusters with 0109 (#213's file, sha256 83f5928e...dea2) added beside this tree, never a real database. (1) Fresh install 0001-0110 by the acceptance runner's migration stage (dry run, migrate, role bootstrap, verify-roles): all 9 database/tests suites and all 67 test/database suites (including outreach-campaign-registration, outreach-session-guards and 0109's support-health-id-matches) passed; 0110's body md5 69469315f04554d2639dfa9f83591d4d and 0109's marker md5 e4f1577e17334abde24784ff9c5c6c66 read back from pg_proc. (2) db:test-staging-schema-upgrade with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS CREATEROLE migrator (local admin URL; baseline 0001-0109 with staging's runtime-grants.sql plus 0109's block): passed, declared [0110], dry run rolled back, applied checksums preserved, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2482), row-level security unchanged (188), no-FORCE baseline passed, clean install passed. (3) On a database migrated 0001-0109 by such a migrator (it owns the trigger function): the outreach suite fails before 0110 (section 1, and with section 1 relaxed the member's campaign registration and resolution are refused 42501); 0110 dry-runs and applies as that migrator; then outreach-campaign-registration and outreach-session-guards pass. Re-running 0110 refuses "0110: already applied"; without 0109's function it refuses "0110: 0001-0109 must be applied first".
